newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends up at three-month high vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends up at three-month high vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at a three-month high of 8.2924 against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2932, supported by positive trade figures, traders said.
China's official media reported today that its trade surplus was $10.29 billion in the first four months, compared with a deficit of $607 million in the same period last year.
The weighted average price on Tuesday was 8.2928.
The news strengthened pro-yuan sentiment, pushing the yuan up further, traders said.
"The market believes that the increased trade surplus will cause more dollar selling and the yuan is expected to rise further," one dealer said.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2925 and moved in a narrow range of 8.2923/8.2925 for most of the session, hitting an intraday high of 8.2921 and a low of 8.2930.
Trading was not active with most done at 8.2924, traders said.
"The trade surplus indicated China's export business has begun to recover, which may bring more demand for the yuan," said another trader.
"If there is no central bank intervention to depress the yuan, the local currency will continue to rise in the short term," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to test the key 8.2920 resistance level on Thursday.
The yuan closed down at 6.9740 from 6.9300 against 100 Japanese yen and lower at 1.0722 from 1.0717 against the Hong Kong dollar.
